summary: The four collections steps each lend themselves to a small ticket function whose result shows the trap the page names (Counter.update adding, _replace leaving the row alone, popitem and move_to_end defaulting to the back, a defaultdict read inserting the key); the two pandas steps do not, because the browser runtime has no pandas.

steps.title: Counter: counting without the bookkeeping
steps.reason: A Counter's counts, its 0 for a missing key and update adding where dict.update replaces all show up in a returned value, and the page names both mistakes. The exercise and demo rung 14 take status_counts over one list, so the task adds up several days of statuses instead.

steps.title: namedtuple: rows whose fields have names
steps.reason: Field access, immutability and _replace returning a new row are all visible on the returned row and on the row passed in, and assigning to a field (the brief's pitfall) raises AttributeError. The exercise's to_rows and the demo's rows() build rows from tickets; the task closes an existing row instead.

steps.title: OrderedDict: when the order is part of the data
steps.reason: move_to_end and popitem change the queue and return a pair a check can read, and leaving out last=False sends the ticket to the back or takes the newest one, which the page shows as the default. The exercise's and demo's work_queue build the order with sorted; the task works on a queue that is already built.

steps.title: The rest of the collections module
steps.reason: The page's named trap, a read of a missing key on a defaultdict inserting it, shows up as the dict's length after the call. The exercise's ids_by_agent and the demo's by_agent build the groups, so the task only reads a defaultdict it is given; deque and ChainMap stay in the notes.

steps.title: pandas: a DataFrame from a JSON file
steps.reason: The browser runtime loads no packages, so pandas, read_json and DataFrame selection cannot run there, and pip and requirements.txt are tools. Faking a DataFrame with plain dicts would practise something the page does not teach.

steps.title: pandas: computed columns, missing values and groups
steps.reason: Computed columns, NaN handling, value_counts, groupby and sort_values all need pandas, which the browser runtime does not load. The one standard-library echo, NaN == NaN being False, is a single comparison and not worth a task.

tasks.title: Counter
tasks.idea: The reader writes week_counts(days), where days is a list of lists of statuses, one list per day, and returns a Counter of every status across all days. For [["open", "closed"], ["open", "assigned"]] the result equals {"open": 2, "closed": 1, "assigned": 1}.
checks: A status seen on two days is counted on both; building a plain dict and calling update with each day's counts keeps only the last day's number.
A status that never appears reads 0 from the result; a plain dict raises KeyError on that read.
An empty list of days gives an empty Counter, equal to {}.
tasks.q: Write week_counts(days). days holds one list of ticket statuses per day, and the function returns a Counter of every status across all the days. For [["open", "closed"], ["open", "assigned"]] it returns a Counter equal to {"open": 2, "closed": 1, "assigned": 1}. Reading a status that never appeared from the result gives 0, and an empty list of days gives an empty Counter.
tasks.tests:
assert week_counts([["open", "closed"], ["open", "assigned"]]) == {"open": 2, "closed": 1, "assigned": 1}, "a status seen on two days is counted on both days"
assert week_counts([["open"], ["closed"]])["escalated"] == 0, "a status that never appears reads 0"
assert week_counts([]) == {}, "no days at all gives an empty count"

tasks.title: namedtuple
tasks.idea: The reader defines TicketRow = namedtuple("TicketRow", ["ticket_id", "priority", "status", "hours"]) and writes close_row(row, hours), which returns a copy of the row with status "closed" and the given hours. close_row(TicketRow(4, "normal", "assigned", None), 22.5) gives TicketRow(4, "normal", "closed", 22.5).
checks: The returned row has status "closed" and hours 22.5, with ticket_id and priority as they were; assigning row.status = "closed" raises AttributeError before anything comes back.
The row passed in still has status "assigned" and hours None afterwards, so the function built a new row.
The result is a TicketRow whose fields sit in the order ticket_id, priority, status, hours, so result[2] is "closed"; returning a dict or a reordered namedtuple fails.
tasks.q: Define TicketRow as a named tuple with the fields ticket_id, priority, status and hours, in that order. Then write close_row(row, hours), which returns a new TicketRow with the same id and priority as row, the status "closed" and the hours it was given. The row passed in stays as it was. close_row(TicketRow(4, "normal", "assigned", None), 22.5) returns TicketRow(4, "normal", "closed", 22.5).
tasks.starter:
from collections import namedtuple

TicketRow = ...


def close_row(row, hours):
    ...
tasks.tests:
row = TicketRow(4, "normal", "assigned", None)
assert TicketRow._fields == ("ticket_id", "priority", "status", "hours"), "TicketRow has the fields ticket_id, priority, status and hours, in that order"
assert close_row(row, 22.5) == TicketRow(4, "normal", "closed", 22.5), "the returned row is closed with the new hours, its id and priority as they were"
assert (row.status, row.hours) == ("assigned", None), "the row passed in still reads assigned with no hours"
assert type(close_row(row, 22.5)) == TicketRow, "close_row returns a TicketRow"

tasks.title: OrderedDict
tasks.idea: The reader writes serve(queue, urgent), where queue is an OrderedDict of ticket id to title, oldest first, and urgent is a ticket id or None. If urgent is given, that ticket moves to the front; then the first pair comes off the queue and is returned. With queue 4, 6, 5 and urgent 5, serve returns (5, "Checkout fails on mobile") and the queue is left as 4, 6.
checks: With urgent 5 the returned pair is ticket 5's; move_to_end(5) without last=False sends it to the back, so another ticket comes off.
With urgent None the oldest ticket, 4, comes off; popitem() with its default last=True takes the newest.
After the call the served ticket is gone and the rest keep their order, so list(queue) is [4, 6] in the first case.
tasks.q: Write serve(queue, urgent). queue is an OrderedDict from ticket id to title, oldest ticket first, and urgent is a ticket id or None. When urgent is a ticket id, move that ticket to the front of the queue. Then take the first pair off the queue and return it as a (ticket id, title) tuple; the tickets left behind keep their order. With a queue holding 4 "Invoice PDF is blank", 6 "Typo on the pricing page" and 5 "Checkout fails on mobile", in that order, serve(queue, 5) returns (5, "Checkout fails on mobile") and leaves list(queue) as [4, 6]. On the same three tickets, serve(queue, None) returns ticket 4's pair.
tasks.tests:
from collections import OrderedDict
first = OrderedDict([(4, "Invoice PDF is blank"), (6, "Typo on the pricing page"), (5, "Checkout fails on mobile")])
second = OrderedDict(first)
assert serve(first, 5) == (5, "Checkout fails on mobile"), "an urgent ticket goes to the front and is served first"
assert list(first) == [4, 6], "the served ticket leaves the queue and the others keep their order"
assert serve(second, None) == (4, "Invoice PDF is blank"), "with no urgent ticket the oldest one is served"

tasks.title: defaultdict
tasks.idea: The reader writes idle_agents(groups, names), where groups is a defaultdict(list) of agent to ticket ids, and returns the names in names that hold no ticket, in the order given. With groups holding Priya: [4, 7] and Marcus: [], idle_agents(groups, ["Priya", "Marcus", "Lee"]) returns ["Marcus", "Lee"].
checks: The result lists the agents with an empty list and the agents missing from groups, in the order of names.
groups still has two keys after the call and "Lee" in groups is False; reading groups[name] to check it inserts Lee with an empty list.
tasks.q: Write idle_agents(groups, names). groups is a defaultdict(list) from agent name to a list of ticket ids, and names is a list of agent names. Return a list of the names in names that hold no ticket, in the order names gives them. An agent holds no ticket when its list is empty or when it is not in groups at all. Leave groups as it was. With groups holding "Priya": [4, 7] and "Marcus": [], idle_agents(groups, ["Priya", "Marcus", "Lee"]) returns ["Marcus", "Lee"].
tasks.tests:
from collections import defaultdict
groups = defaultdict(list, {"Priya": [4, 7], "Marcus": []})
assert idle_agents(groups, ["Priya", "Marcus", "Lee"]) == ["Marcus", "Lee"], "lists the agents with an empty list and the agents missing from groups"
assert list(groups) == ["Priya", "Marcus"], "groups still holds only Priya and Marcus; checking Lee does not add Lee"
assert idle_agents(groups, ["Lee", "Priya", "Marcus"]) == ["Lee", "Marcus"], "keeps the order the names come in"
